newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state to maintain Banerj's base price.
newsitem.headline: Rio state to maintain Banerj's base price.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state government will revise the privatization rules for its state bank Banerj but it does not plan to change its minimum price, Rio's Planning Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar said.
"We will revise the whole privatization process, but our intention is to keep the minimum price unchanged," Alencar told a news conference.
The minimum price for Banerj and its insurance subsidiary Banerj Seguros, whose sale has been postponed twice already, is 480 million reais.

Alencar said he will hold talks with all interested investors, including those who dropped out of the sell-off, before a new tender document with the revised privatization rules is published in January.
He also said he backs the idea of reopening the period for pre-qualification of investors so as to attract new bidders for Banerj's sale.
Only two -- Bradesco and Banco Itau -- of eight investors who had pre-qualified for the sell-off had signed up for the auction.
Alencar said the new tender document will be published to eliminate all doubts surrounding Banerj's sale.

He said the tender details will include the 2.0 billion real guarantee fund which will be created by the state government to cover the bank's debts including those owed to its pension fund and employees.
The fund will be created under a refinancing package for Rio de Janeiro state's 9.0 billion real debt currently being negotiated with the federal government, Alencar said.

Alencar also said the liquidation of Banerj's bad debts, ordered by the Central Bank today, will facilitate the sale process of the financially healthy section of Banerj, formally known as Banco Banerj S.A., which is the object of the privatization.
Banerj was split earlier this year into two units -- Banco do Estado do Rio de Janeiro to include its unrecoverable assets and Banco Banerj S.A. for its regular banking operations.
The Planning Secretary emphasized the sale of Banco Banerj S.A. is irreversible, adding that the bank will not return to state hands.
Since early January Banerj has been managed by private bank Bozano, Simonsen to ready it for sell-off on behalf of the Central Bank, which took over the bank in December 1994.
On Friday, the Central Bank announced it was extending for a further 180 days its administration of Banco Banerj S.A.
Bozano, Simonsen will continue administering the bank on behalf of the Central Bank, Alencar said.
He also said Bozano will be in charge of the liquidation of Banco do Estado do Rio de Janeiro.
